questions.explanation: Starch is a polysaccharide made of alpha glucose monomers joined by glycosidic bonds. It exists in two forms: amylose (unbranched) and amylopectin (branched).

questions.stem: Why is glycogen described as a good energy storage molecule in animals?

options.text: It is a very small molecule
It is highly branched, allowing rapid release of glucose when energy is needed

questions.explanation: Glycogen is highly branched, which provides many endpoints from which glucose molecules can be quickly removed by enzymes when energy is needed, such as during exercise.
Cellulose is made of beta glucose monomers. The beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds create straight chains that form hydrogen bonds between parallel chains, creating strong microfibrils.

questions.stem: Why can humans not digest cellulose?

options.text: Cellulose is too large to enter the body
Humans lack the enzyme cellulase needed to break beta glycosidic bonds

questions.explanation: Humans lack the enzyme cellulase that is needed to break the beta-1,4 glycosidic bonds in cellulose. This is why cellulose acts as dietary fibre rather than an energy source.

questions.stem: What is the structural difference between amylose and amylopectin?

options.text: Amylose is made of beta glucose and amylopectin of alpha glucose
Amylose is branched and amylopectin is straight
Amylose is an unbranched helix and amylopectin is branched

questions.explanation: Amylose is an unbranched chain that coils into a helix, while amylopectin has a branched structure with 1,6 glycosidic bonds at branch points in addition to 1,4 bonds.

questions.stem: Where is glycogen mainly stored in the human body?
questions.explanation: Glycogen is mainly stored in the liver and skeletal muscles. Liver glycogen helps maintain blood glucose levels, while muscle glycogen provides energy for muscle contraction.

questions.stem: Why is starch insoluble in water?

options.text: It is too small to interact with water
Its coiled and branched structure makes it compact and unable to dissolve

questions.explanation: Starch is insoluble because the amylose chains coil into helices and the large amylopectin molecules fold compactly. This insolubility is important because it means starch does not affect water potential in cells.
